editorial:
Imagine living in a quiet little town back in 1910 where nothing ever happens. You meet Jacob, a shy book store owner who has his life totally figured out. His biggest highlight of the week is heading to the local club to bathe with his buddies every Sunday. He isn't really looking for love or interested in women at all, until Amelie Arbel rolls into town. She has money, she is gorgeous, and she knows exactly how to get Jacob's attention. It feels like a cozy, slow-burn romance at first, but once they get married, the vibe shifts into a funny and stressful mess.

What really makes this work is seeing Jacob's world get turned upside down by his new wife. Amelie is a handful, and watching him try to handle her drama is the best part of the film. The acting is great, though the pace is a bit slow in the middle. If you like old-school comedies about marriage mishaps, you will love this. You should definitely try renting it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you are a movie buff, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: By the end, Jacob realizes that marrying Amelie was a huge mistake. Her constant demands and wild personality completely exhaust him. After a series of funny but stressful fights, Jacob decides he cannot handle the chaos anymore. He chooses his peace of mind over the flashy lifestyle Amelie offers. He eventually returns to his simple life and his Sunday bathing routine, happy to be back in his quiet world without the drama.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old-fashioned comedies and stories about mismatched couples.
